claim: The airway epithelium is composed of myriad distinct cell types, many of which have only been recently described.
source: The airway epithelium is composed of myriad distinct cell types, many of which have only been recently described (Deprez et al., 2020; Goldfarbmuren et al., 2020; Montoro et al., 2018; Plasschaert et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to recent literature describing airway epithelial cell types

claim: NADH and NADPH cannot be distinguished by their autofluorescence.
source: Since NADH and NADPH cannot be distinguished by their autofluorescence, the combination has been reported as an aggregate quantity, NAD(P)H (Schaefer et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Schaefer et al., 2019

claim: A metabolic ratio of FAD/(NAD[P]H+FAD) is often employed to account for the effects of light scattering and variation in the number of mitochondria.
source: To account for the effects of light scattering and variation in the number of mitochondria, a metabolic ratio of FAD/(NAD[P]H+FAD) is often employed (Chance et al., 1979).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chance et al., 1979

claim: Two-photon excited fluorescence microscopy can be used to measure the metabolic ratio in intact tissues and in vivo.
source: Two-photon excited fluorescence microscopy can be used to measure this metabolic ratio in intact tissues and in vivo (Dilipkumar et al., 2019; Klinger et al., 2012; Kreiß et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies demonstrating this technique

claim: Common intestinal epithelial cell types can be distinguished based on their morphology when imaged using two-photon microscopy.
source: Indeed, abundant common intestinal epithelial cell types can be distinguished based on their morphology when imaged in this manner (Kreiß et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kreiß et al., 2020

claim: Measures of metabolic activity have been used to identify immune cells in differing functional states during fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) ex vivo.
source: Most recently, these measures of metabolic activity have been used to identify immune cells in differing functional states during fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) ex vivo (Lemire et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lemire et al., 2022

claim: Immune cell interactions have been visualized using autofluorescence in the murine trachea.
source: Furthermore, immune cell interactions have been visualized using autofluorescence in the murine trachea (Kretschmer et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kretschmer et al., 2016

claim: Treatment with rotenone and antimycin A leads to a decrease in the FAD/(NAD[P]H+FAD) fluorescence ratio at the airway surface.
source: Treatment with rotenone and antimycin A, inhibitors of mitochondrial complex I and complex III, lead to a decrease in the FAD/(NAD[P]H+FAD) fluorescence ratio at the airway surface as predicted from similar experiments conducted in breast cancer cells (Figure 1C; Hou et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and citation to similar experiments in Hou et al., 2016

claim: Treatment with FCCP leads to an increase in autofluorescence intensity ratio.
source: Treatment with FCCP, a mitochondrial uncoupler, led to an anticipated increase in autofluorescence intensity ratio, as similarly previously documented (Figure 1D; Hou et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and citation to Hou et al., 2016

claim: The autofluorescence signal remained stable over 2 days of tracheal explant culture.
source: In order to determine signal stability, we measured the autofluorescence intensity ratio over 2 days of tracheal explant culture. The signal remained stable (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E

claim: Ciliated cells have a robust FAD signal which is primarily located near the luminal cell surface.
source: As seen in Figure 2A, ciliated cells have a robust FAD signal which is primarily located near the luminal cell surface.
evidence: Supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2A

claim: Secretory cells demonstrate a more robust NADH signal in contrast to ciliated cells.
source: Secretory cells demonstrated a more robust NADH signal (Figure 2B) that was in sharp contrast to that of ciliated cells.
evidence: Supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2B

claim: Ciliated, secretory, and basal cells can be distinguished by their autofluorescence ratios.
source: These differences in autofluorescence ratio can be quantified for the individual cell types and can be used to distinguish ciliated, secretory, and basal cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2D

claim: Ciliated and secretory cells could still be distinguished following the application of mitochondrial poisons, although the ratios were less well separated.
source: Ciliated and secretory cells could still be distinguished following the application of the aforementioned mitochondrial poisons (Figure 1C and D), although the ratios were less well separated (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C, D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: Chemical or physiologic perturbations may alter the ability to distinguish cell types based on their autofluorescence ratios alone.
source: This suggests that chemical or physiologic perturbations may alter the ability to distinguish cell types based on their autofluorescence ratios alone.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that mitochondrial poisons reduce separation of autofluorescence ratios

claim: The unique polygonal cell shape of hillock cells and discrete boundaries of hillocks are easily distinguishable with autofluorescence imaging.
source: The unique polygonal cell shape of hillock cells and discrete boundaries of hillocks are easily distinguishable with autofluorescence imaging.
evidence: Based on observations from autofluorescence imaging

claim: Ionocytes have puncta of high FAD signal toward the apical aspect of the cell.
source: Additionally, ionocytes were found to have puncta of high FAD signal toward the apical aspect of the cell (Figure 3Biv).
evidence: Supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3Biv

claim: Neuroendocrine cells display the lowest NAD(P)H and FAD autofluorescence of all airway epithelial cells.
source: Of all airway epithelial cells, neuroendocrine cells labeled by PGP9 (cyan) displayed the lowest NAD(P)H and FAD autofluorescence (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3D

claim: Rare cells are characterized by very similar autofluorescence intensity ratios and could not be distinguished by this criterion alone.
source: Interestingly, as an aggregate, rare cells are characterized by very similar autofluorescence intensity ratios and could not be distinguished by this criterion alone (Figure 3E).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3E

claim: Autofluorescence intensity ratio and morphological differences allow the separation of all airway epithelial cell types into distinct clusters.
source: In aggregate, these characteristics allowed the separation of all airway epithelial cell types into distinct clusters (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by UMAP clustering analysis shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 2

claim: K-nearest neighbor analysis and multinomial logistic regression resulted in 96% accuracy for cell type classification.
source: K-nearest neighbor analysis and multinomial logistic regression resulted in 96% accuracy, while XGBoost performed with 92% accuracy.
evidence: Supported by machine learning algorithm performance data

claim: XGBoost performed with 92% accuracy for cell type classification.
source: K-nearest neighbor analysis and multinomial logistic regression resulted in 96% accuracy, while XGBoost performed with 92% accuracy.
evidence: Supported by machine learning algorithm performance data

claim: Nuclear position, aspect YZ, NADH autofluorescence, ratio of deviation, and FAD autofluorescence are the most important characteristics for cell type assignment.
source: We then established the weight that each characteristic contributes to cell type-specific identification when using a XGBoost machine learning algorithm (Table 1), which shows that nuclear position, aspect YZ, NADH autofluorescence, ratio of deviation, and FAD autofluorescence are the most important characteristics for cell type assignment.
evidence: Supported by XGBoost feature importance analysis shown in Table 1

claim: Upon excluding autofluorescence and using morphometric criteria alone, the accuracy and model quality are dramatically reduced.
source: Upon excluding autofluorescence and using morphometric criteria alone, the accuracy and model quality as measured by a Matthews Correlation Coefficient are dramatically reduced, highlighting the importance of obtaining autofluorescence signatures for cell type identification (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by machine learning performance data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4

claim: Cholinergic and adrenergic stimulation have historically been known to cause airway secretory cell granule release.
source: Cholinergic and adrenergic stimulation have historically been known to cause airway secretory cell granule release (Massaro et al., 1979; Yoneda, 1977).
evidence: Supported by citations to historical studies

claim: CCSP is a major constituent of secretory cell granules and is commonly used to assign secretory cell identity.
source: The club cell secretory protein, CCSP (also known as CC10, Uteroglobin, CC16, and SCGB1A1), is a major constituent of these granules and is commonly used to assign secretory cell identity (Wong et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wong et al., 2009

claim: Methacholine stimulation led to a 70% decrease in the CCSP immunofluorescence staining as measured by fluorescence intensity relative to time zero.
source: Methacholine stimulation led to a 70% decrease in the CCSP immunofluorescence staining as measured by fluorescence intensity relative to time zero (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A-B

claim: Methacholine stimulation leads to a dramatically diminished ability to identify secretory cells using CCSP staining.
source: Indeed, this stimulus-induced reduction in CCSP, classically considered a specific cell type marker, leads to a dramatically diminished ability to identify secretory cells.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that CCSP staining decreases after methacholine stimulation

claim: Autofluorescence intensity ratios continue to discriminate secretory cells after methacholine stimulation.
source: Methacholine stimulation also alters NAD(P)H and FAD fluorescence intensities; however, these autofluorescence intensity ratios continue to discriminate secretory cells (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C-D

claim: Methacholine stimulation results in the development of non-fluorescent spherical 'voids' within secretory cells.
source: To our surprise, we found that methacholine stimulation resulted in the development of non-fluorescent spherical 'voids' within secretory cells (Figure 4C boxes, further magnification of these boxes in Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4C and 4E

claim: 'Voids' were present in approximately 9% of secretory cells prior to stimulation.
source: We performed detailed examination of the field in Figure 4C and found that 'voids' were present in approximately 9% of secretory cells prior to stimulation, but the fraction of secretory cells with 'voids' dramatically increased to 78% following methacholine stimulation (Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of imaging data

claim: The fraction of secretory cells with 'voids' dramatically increased to 78% following methacholine stimulation.
source: We performed detailed examination of the field in Figure 4C and found that 'voids' were present in approximately 9% of secretory cells prior to stimulation, but the fraction of secretory cells with 'voids' dramatically increased to 78% following methacholine stimulation (Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of imaging data

claim: Intestinal secretory and goblet cells internalize luminal contents, resulting in the formation of SAPs and GAPs.
source: Indeed, such a sampling process has been demonstrated in the gut epithelium during which secretory and goblet cells internalize luminal contents. In this case, internalization results in the formation of SAPs and GAPs within the intestinal secretory and goblet cells (Gustafsson and Johansson, 2022; McDole et al., 2012; Noah et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to studies on intestinal epithelium

claim: Airway secretory cells adopt a goblet cell morphology within hours.
source: Given that airway secretory cells adopt a goblet cell morphology within hours, airway SAPs and GAPs are likely equivalent (Evans et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Evans et al., 2004

claim: Airway SAPs and GAPs are likely equivalent.
source: Given that airway secretory cells adopt a goblet cell morphology within hours, airway SAPs and GAPs are likely equivalent (Evans et al., 2004).
evidence: Inferred from the morphological similarity between airway secretory cells and goblet cells

claim: Upon stimulation with methacholine, secretory cells show uptake of FITC-dextran that is clearly distinguishable from the nucleus.
source: To definitely evaluate our hypothesis concerning the origin of the spherical autofluorescence 'voids' in our system, we incubated tracheal explants cultures in 10Kd FITC-dextran. Upon stimulation with methacholine, secretory cells showed uptake of FITC-dextran that was clearly distinguishable from the nucleus (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A

claim: The 'voids' are membrane bound structures containing FITC-dextran.
source: Since autofluorescence imaging alone cannot be used to establish the presence of a membrane, we resorted to employing epithelia expressing membrane tdTomato to assess whether the 'voids' were membrane bound. Indeed, we found uptake of FITC-dextran into membrane encapsulated structures delineated by membrane tdTomato (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B using membrane tdTomato

claim: Uptake of dextran occurs both in unstimulated and methacholine stimulated samples, though is dramatically exaggerated following stimulation with methacholine.
source: This uptake of dextran occurs both in unstimulated and methacholine stimulated samples, though is dramatically exaggerated following stimulation with methacholine (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C

claim: The increased SAP formation following stimulation with methacholine recapitulates the induction of intestinal GAPs following cholinergic stimulation.
source: The increased SAP formation following stimulation with methacholine recapitulates the induction of intestinal GAPs following cholinergic stimulation (Knoop et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Knoop et al., 2015 showing similar phenomenon in intestine

claim: Live imaging over 60 min demonstrates the uptake of FITC-dextran into the cell from the apical surface, further accumulation of FITC-dextran into the cell, and a major secretion event.
source: Live imaging over 60 min demonstrates the uptake of FITC-dextran into the cell from the apical surface, further accumulation of FITC-dextran into the cell, and a major secretion event (Figure 5D and Figure 5—videos 1–3, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 5D and associated videos

claim: Airway secretory cells with SAPs containing either FITC-dextran or FITC-ovalbumin closely associate with CD11c+APCs that had been recruited to the airway epithelium following an LPS challenge.
source: Additionally, further mirroring their gut counterparts, airway secretory cells with SAPs containing either FITC-dextran or FITC-ovalbumin closely associate with CD11c+APCs that had been recruited to the airway epithelium following an LPS challenge (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 2; McDole et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2

claim: Many LPS-stimulated APCs are intraepithelial and possess dendriform processes that extend toward SAPs.
source: Many of these LPS-stimulated APCs are intraepithelial and possess dendriform processes that extend toward SAPs.
evidence: Based on observations from imaging data

claim: Airway SAPs are likely to play an important role in the immunologic response to antigens present in the airway lumen.
source: This suggests that airway SAPs are likely to play an important role in the immunologic response to antigens present in the airway lumen.
evidence: Inferred from the association of SAPs with APCs

claim: Markers of cell type such as the secretory cell marker CCSP can be misleading when used for the enumeration of cell numbers in COPD patient samples.
source: This may be of particular relevance to disease states since it has been noted that markers of cell type such as the secretory cell marker CCSP can be misleading when used for the enumeration of cell numbers in COPD patient samples (Pilette et al., 2001), in asthma (Shijubo et al., 1999), and in smokers (Shijubo et al., 1997) presumably due to the fact that CCSP has been secreted into the lumen.
evidence: Supported by citation to Pilette et al., 2001

claim: CCSP can be misleading when used for the enumeration of cell numbers in asthma.
source: This may be of particular relevance to disease states since it has been noted that markers of cell type such as the secretory cell marker CCSP can be misleading when used for the enumeration of cell numbers in COPD patient samples (Pilette et al., 2001), in asthma (Shijubo et al., 1999), and in smokers (Shijubo et al., 1997) presumably due to the fact that CCSP has been secreted into the lumen.
evidence: Supported by citation to Shijubo et al., 1999

claim: CCSP can be misleading when used for the enumeration of cell numbers in smokers.
source: This may be of particular relevance to disease states since it has been noted that markers of cell type such as the secretory cell marker CCSP can be misleading when used for the enumeration of cell numbers in COPD patient samples (Pilette et al., 2001), in asthma (Shijubo et al., 1999), and in smokers (Shijubo et al., 1997) presumably due to the fact that CCSP has been secreted into the lumen.
evidence: Supported by citation to Shijubo et al., 1997

claim: Infection and inflammation may alter autofluorescence.
source: However, despite its advantages, it should be noted that infection and inflammation may alter autofluorescence (Dilipkumar et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dilipkumar et al., 2019

claim: Using a new fixation procedure, luminal dextran uptake has been documented in murine airway goblet and secretory cells, suggestive of GAPs.
source: Recently, using a new fixation procedure, luminal dextran uptake has been documented in murine airway goblet and secretory cells, suggestive of GAPs (Tang et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tang et al., 2022

claim: Intestinal GAPs play a role in immune tolerance.
source: Intestinal GAPs play a role in immune tolerance (Knoop et al., 2017; Knoop et al., 2020), the imprinting of dendritic cells (Kulkarni et al., 2020), and participate in inflammatory disease (Knoop et al., 2017; Knoop et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Knoop et al., 2017 and 2020

claim: Intestinal GAPs play a role in the imprinting of dendritic cells.
source: Intestinal GAPs play a role in immune tolerance (Knoop et al., 2017; Knoop et al., 2020), the imprinting of dendritic cells (Kulkarni et al., 2020), and participate in inflammatory disease (Knoop et al., 2017; Knoop et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kulkarni et al., 2020

claim: Intestinal GAPs participate in inflammatory disease.
source: Intestinal GAPs play a role in immune tolerance (Knoop et al., 2017; Knoop et al., 2020), the imprinting of dendritic cells (Kulkarni et al., 2020), and participate in inflammatory disease (Knoop et al., 2017; Knoop et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Knoop et al., 2017 and 2020

claim: Analogous phenomenon to intestinal GAPs has been documented to occur in the case of goblet cells of the eye.
source: Analogous phenomenon has been documented to occur in the case of goblet cells of the eye (Barbosa et al., 2017; Ko et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Barbosa et al., 2017 and Ko et al., 2018

claim: Autofluorescence imaging permits label-free cell type assignment in airway epithelium.
source: We report a non-invasive imaging modality that capitalizes on the endogenous autofluorescence signatures of the metabolic cofactors NAD(P)H and FAD. By marrying morphological characteristics with autofluorescence signatures, all seven of the airway epithelial cell types can be distinguished simultaneously in mouse tracheal explants in real time.
evidence: Supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript

claim: All seven of the airway epithelial cell types can be distinguished simultaneously in mouse tracheal explants in real time using autofluorescence and morphology.
source: By marrying morphological characteristics with autofluorescence signatures, all seven of the airway epithelial cell types can be distinguished simultaneously in mouse tracheal explants in real time.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing identification of all seven cell types

claim: This methodology for direct cell type-specific identification avoids pitfalls associated with the use of ostensibly cell type-specific markers that are altered by clinically relevant physiologic stimuli.
source: Furthermore, we find that this methodology for direct cell type-specific identification avoids pitfalls associated with the use of ostensibly cell type-specific markers that are, in fact, altered by clinically relevant physiologic stimuli.
evidence: Supported by data showing CCSP loss after methacholine stimulation while autofluorescence signatures remain

claim: Dynamic secretory cell associated antigen passages (SAPs) form in response to cholinergic stimulus in the airway.
source: Finally, we utilize this methodology to interrogate real-time physiology and identify dynamic secretory cell associated antigen passages (SAPs) that form in response to cholinergic stimulus.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing SAP formation after methacholine stimulation

claim: The identical process of dynamic SAP/GAP formation has been well documented in the intestine where it enables luminal antigen sampling.
source: The identical process has been well documented in the intestine where the dynamic formation of SAPs and goblet cell associated antigen passages (GAPs) enable luminal antigen sampling.
evidence: Supported by references to intestinal literature

claim: Airway secretory cells with SAPs are frequently juxtaposed to antigen presenting cells.
source: Airway secretory cells with SAPs are frequently juxtaposed to antigen presenting cells, suggesting that airway SAPs, like their intestinal counterparts, not only sample antigen but convey their cargo for immune cell processing.
evidence: Supported by imaging data showing association between SAPs and CD11c+ APCs

claim: Airway SAPs, like their intestinal counterparts, not only sample antigen but convey their cargo for immune cell processing.
source: Airway secretory cells with SAPs are frequently juxtaposed to antigen presenting cells, suggesting that airway SAPs, like their intestinal counterparts, not only sample antigen but convey their cargo for immune cell processing.
evidence: Inferred from the juxtaposition of SAPs with APCs and comparison to intestinal GAPs

claim: Current techniques for cell type identification require the use of fluorescent genetic reporters that only allow the study of three or four cell types at a time.
source: Current techniques require the use of fluorescent genetic reporters that are not only cumbersome, but which only allow the study of three or four cell types at a time.
evidence: Based on general knowledge of current fluorescent reporter limitations

claim: Post-fixation cell identification is destructive and precludes the study of long-term processes or the effect of multiple serial stimuli.
source: Since post-fixation cell identification is destructive, it also precludes the study of long-term processes or the effect of multiple serial stimuli which are both essential features of normal organ physiology.
evidence: Based on logical reasoning about the limitations of destructive techniques

claim: Markers used for cell type identification in unperturbed tissue can often be non-specific or misleading after injury.
source: Additionally, markers used for cell type identification in unperturbed tissue can often be non-specific or misleading after injury.
evidence: Based on observations from the literature and experimental data showing CCSP loss

claim: Label-free imaging based on endogenous fluorescence of metabolic cofactors has been deployed to measure cell metabolism in various tissues, particularly in tumors and immune cells.
source: Label-free imaging based on endogenous fluorescence of metabolic cofactors has been deployed to measure cell metabolism in various tissues, particularly in tumors and immune cells (Katz et al., 2002; Skala et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Katz et al., 2002 and Skala et al., 2007

claim: NADH, NADPH, and FAD have been used to monitor metabolism in vitro and in vivo.
source: NADH, NADPH, and FAD, the major endogenous fluorophores, have been used to monitor metabolism in vitro and in vivo (Gil et al., 2019; Heikal, 2010; Huang et al., 2002; Kasischke et al., 2004; Rocheleau et al., 2004; Sepehr et al., 2012; Tiede et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to studies using these fluorophores

claim: The samples were scanned at 730 nm and 900 nm sequentially to facilitate optimal detection and separation of NAD(P)H and FAD.
source: To facilitate optimal detection and separation of NAD(P)H and FAD, the samples were scanned at 730 nm and 900 nm sequentially (Huang et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to Huang et al., 2002 and described methodology

claim: Second harmonic generation (SHG) imaging of collagen fibers was used to identify the basement membrane.
source: To accomplish this, we utilized second harmonic generation (SHG) imaging of collagen fibers to identify the basement membrane (SHG signal was excited with a 900 nm laser) and developed a MATLAB algorithm to 'flatten' the epithelial surface (https://github.com/vss11/Label-free-autofluorescence, copy archived at Shah, 2023).
evidence: Described in the methods section

claim: A MATLAB algorithm was developed to 'flatten' the epithelial surface.
source: To accomplish this, we utilized second harmonic generation (SHG) imaging of collagen fibers to identify the basement membrane (SHG signal was excited with a 900 nm laser) and developed a MATLAB algorithm to 'flatten' the epithelial surface (https://github.com/vss11/Label-free-autofluorescence, copy archived at Shah, 2023).
evidence: Described in the methods section with code repository reference
